claims.statement: NIS2 introduces cybersecurity risk-management and incident-reporting requirements across more sectors; affected entities currently spend on controls, audits and remediation.
The framework covers 18 critical sectors and includes supply-chain security among required elements, but national scope and enforcement must be checked for each Polish customer.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: CISO, IT director, risk director or managing board
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: A fixed-duration evidence sprint outputs board-ready ownership and proof, complementing rather than replacing security tools.
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The prospective business would own sprint contracts; clients retain control evidence and security decisions.
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Managed-service providers and cyber-audit firms refer clients that are not ready for full consulting projects.

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Assumption: 5,000-12,000 PLN per customer through partners.
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Fifty percent upfront and remainder on evidence-pack delivery.
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Professional liability, secure workspace, legal and accounting estimated at 15,000 PLN monthly.
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Fixed-price sprint plus quarterly evidence refresh.
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Contract security specialist, scanning tools and evidence review.

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Cyber consultancies can offer similar assessments; productized scope, rapid delivery and partner-friendly handoff differentiate.
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Affected organization pays for a fixed evidence sprint or incurs staff and remediation costs when it cannot demonstrate risk-management controls.
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Board request, customer questionnaire, audit or incident.
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Quarterly evidence refresh and annual reassessment.

contrary_evidence: NIS2 implementation and customer scope vary by member state.
The founder lacks stated cybersecurity credentials and must partner with qualified specialists.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Unknown; proposed client evidence-access agreement and cyber-specialist subcontract are unsigned.
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Sell a low-risk readiness inventory using client-entered evidence and partner for all technical assurance.
critical_control_point.current_owner: Clients own security evidence; qualified cybersecurity firms control specialist capacity.
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The prospective business would own sprint contracts; clients retain control evidence and security decisions.
critical_control_point.duration: Unknown until project contracts are signed.
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No existing client evidence rights or specialist capacity contracts.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: The founder would control project orchestration; specialists control technical judgments and clients approve remediation.
critical_control_point.renewal: Unknown; proposed project plus quarterly refresh.
critical_control_point.subject: Cybersecurity control-evidence workflow

economics.acquisition_route: Subcontract a qualified cyber lead, sell ten narrowly scoped evidence inventories, then standardize recurring refreshes.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 180 sprints annually at 35,000 PLN plus refresh subscriptions yields about 7M PLN revenue; at 15% owner earnings and a 5x service value, a 70% stake could exceed 5M PLN in years 7-10. Specialist leverage and sales cycles are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 15 hours weekly focused on automation and delivery orchestration.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Project revenue less direct specialist and tooling cost; target 52%.
economics.payback: Customer compares 25,000-50,000 PLN sprint cost with internal audit labor and remediation delay; quantify in pilots.
economics.pricing: 25,000-50,000 PLN sprint plus 2,000-5,000 PLN monthly refresh.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Controls, personnel and evidence change continuously.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned evidence mappings and remediation-duration benchmarks.
fingerprint.customer: Mid-market Polish entities in NIS2 sectors or pressured supply chains.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Fixed-price evidence sprint with recurring refresh.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Risk or IT budget pays on sprint kickoff and evidence delivery.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Audit, board request, customer questionnaire or incident.

founder_fit: Project automation and analytical mapping fit
Part-time orchestration is plausible after scoping

structure.critical_dependency: Qualified cyber judgment and client evidence access

thesis: Productize the evidence-assembly bottleneck created by cybersecurity risk obligations while contracting, rather than pretending to own, specialist assurance.
title: NIS2 Evidence Sprint
uncertainties: Boundary between readiness support and assurance
